question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Probability Given a Normal Distribution Model
question.problem:
The heights (in meters) of the trees in a particular park are normally distributed with a mean of $9\,\text{m}$ and a standard deviation of $4\,\text{m}.$ Assuming that the heights of the trees in the park are normally distributed, what is the probability that a randomly selected tree is less than $10\,\text{m}$ tall? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ | $\,0.5596\,$ | $\,0.5636\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ | $\,0.5987\,$ | $\,0.6026\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6331\,$ | $\,0.6368\,$ | $\,0.6406\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the heights (in meters) of the trees in the park. Then we have $X∼N(9,{4}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X<10).$ First, we write this as a cumulative probability:

$$
P(X<10)=P(X\le 10)
$$

Then, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 10) & =P(Z\le \frac{10-9}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.25) \\  & =Φ(0.25)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.25)=0.5987≈0.60.
$$

Therefore, the probability of a randomly selected tree being shorter than $10\,\text{m}$ is approximately $0.60.$
